summary.intent: Redesign the memory loop TUI to display top navigation as styled tabs and filter options as card-style chips, improving visual hierarchy and aesthetics.
summary.outcome: Successfully implemented a two-row tab bar with an 'MEMORY LOOP' app title and amber underline indicator, uppercase chip-style filter buttons with active/inactive states, and a 'DETAILS' section header above the detail pane. All tests passed and changes were committed.

repo: The memorylooptui package uses a Bubble Tea TUI with separate files per tab: tab_memories.go, tab_settings.go, render.go, styles.go, root.go
The Settings tab already had amber chip-style filter rendering that served as a reference pattern for the Memories tab redesign

render_test.go was an untracked file written in anticipation of the redesign — the strings it tested ('MEMORY LOOP', 'ACTIVE', 'CANDIDATE', 'DETAILS') did not exist in the codebase before this session
contentHeight() in root.go must be updated whenever the tab bar gains or loses a row, or layout will be off

code.finding: Added 5 new style fields: appTitle, tabUnderline, filterChipActive, filterChipInactive, sectionHeader
renderTabBar redesigned to two rows: title + tab labels on row 1, amber underline beneath active tab on row 2
Filter labels uppercased; renderFilterBar now renders chip-style buttons; renderDetail now prepends a 'DETAILS' section header; no-color fallback uses [brackets]
contentHeight() decremented by 1 extra to account for the new second row in the tab bar

workflow: Checking an existing similar component (Settings tab) before implementing a new UI pattern is an effective way to ensure visual consistency
Grepping for test fixture strings in the codebase is a reliable way to detect whether a test was written ahead of implementation vs. for existing behavior

friction: The render_test.go file tested strings that didn't exist in the codebase yet, causing confusion about whether the test was failing or written for a future state — required grep investigation to resolve
Multiple sequential edits were needed to tab_memories.go to build up the renderDetail changes incrementally, suggesting the function had tightly coupled logic
open_items: The 'No ACTIVE memories' empty-state message now uses uppercase filter names, which reads slightly awkwardly — may want to revisit for grammatical clarity
The render_test.go was untracked before this session; worth confirming it is now tracked and passing in CI as a permanent regression guard
